# 1. Offer letter

**BRIGHTWATER ANALYTICS, INC.**
Austin, Texas

November 10, 2025

John Stiles
San Diego, California

**Re: Offer of Employment**

Dear John,

We are pleased to offer you employment with Brightwater Analytics, Inc. (the "Company") on the terms below.

**1. Position**
You will be a **Software Engineer II (L4)**, a full-time, exempt position, reporting to Mary Major, Engineering Manager. You will work remotely from your home in California.

**2. Compensation**
Your annual base salary will be **[$175,000 – BASE SALARY PENDING APPROVAL]**, paid in accordance with the Company's regular payroll schedule and subject to applicable withholdings.

**3. Equity**
Subject to the Company's equity plan and award agreement, you will receive **[3,200 – RSU COUNT PENDING APPROVAL]** restricted stock units. They vest over four years, with a one-year cliff: no units vest until your first anniversary of employment, and the remainder vests thereafter on the schedule in your award agreement. Vesting requires continued employment.

**4. Signing bonus**
You will receive a one-time signing bonus of **$20,000**, less applicable withholdings, payable in your first regular paycheck. If you resign voluntarily within 12 months of your start date, you must repay a pro-rated portion of the bonus. The portion is the gross bonus multiplied by (12 minus the number of full months you worked) ÷ 12. The Company will not deduct any repayment from your final wages unless you separately authorize it in writing.

**5. Start date**
Your anticipated start date is **Monday, December 1, 2025**, subject to Section 7.

**6. Benefits**
You will be eligible to participate in the Company's benefit programs on the terms described in the Brightwater Benefits Guide, as amended from time to time.

**7. Contingencies**
This offer is contingent on (a) satisfactory completion of a background check and (b) your providing proof of identity and authorization to work in the United States within the time required by law.

**8. At-will employment**
Your employment is at will. Either you or the Company may end it at any time, with or without cause or notice. Only a written agreement signed by an authorized Company officer can change this.

**9. Governing law**
This letter is governed by California law. Any dispute arising from it will be resolved in the state or federal courts located in California.

**10. Acceptance**
This offer expires at 5:00 p.m. Central on **November 14, 2025**. To accept, sign and date below. This letter is the complete statement of the terms of your offer and supersedes any earlier verbal discussions.

Sincerely,

[Name, Title], Brightwater Analytics, Inc.

**Accepted and agreed:**
_______________________ John Stiles  Date: ____________

---

# 2. Cover note to Mary Major

**Subject: John Stiles offer (REQ-2291): hold before sending**

Mary, the verbal offer on Nov 7 differed from the approved requisition in five places. The draft letter uses approved terms only.

| Item | Promised | Approved | Recommendation / sign-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Title | Senior SWE | SWE II (L4) | Use L4. A Senior title or level needs a revised requisition (VP Eng + Finance). |
| Base | $182,000 | Max $175,000 | Offer $175,000, or seek a $7,000 exception (VP Eng + Finance). Placeholder in letter. |
| RSUs | 4,000 | 3,200 | Offer 3,200, or seek an increase (Compensation Committee). Placeholder in letter. |
| Non-compete | 12 months, U.S. | n/a | **Removed.** Void for a California employee under B&P §16600, and he asked to drop it. "Standard" was wrong for California. **Legal to confirm.** |
| Governing law | Texas / Travis County | n/a | Changed to California law and venue, since Labor Code §925 bars the Texas clause. **Legal to confirm.** |

Also changed: the template's full-repayment signing-bonus clause. It is now pro-rated by full months, with no deduction from final wages without separate written authorization, per California practice. The $20,000 is within the approved "up to" amount.

**Next steps**
1. Please decide by **Nov 12** whether to pursue the base and RSU exceptions. Without approval, the letter goes out at $175,000 and 3,200 RSUs.
2. Because John accepted verbally at higher numbers, someone (you or the recruiter) should call him before the letter arrives and explain the differences.
3. Legal should review the final letter. The Dec 1 start is tight if the background check isn't cleared, so I will confirm timing with the recruiter.

---

# 3. Worked example: signing-bonus repayment

**Facts:** $20,000 bonus, 12-month pro-rated repayment, John resigns voluntarily after 7 full months.

- Months not worked: 12 − 7 = 5
- Repayment: $20,000 × 5/12 = **$8,333.33**
- Amount John keeps: $20,000 − $8,333.33 = $11,666.67

The Company would invoice John for the $8,333.33. It could not take it from his final paycheck unless he signed a separate written authorization. Under the unmodified template he would have owed the full $20,000. Payroll should confirm how the gross-versus-net tax treatment applies to the repayment.
